assistant|route_option_yellowstone_loop: Suggested Option 1: head west on I-90 to Jackson, Wyoming (approx. 18 hours), then Grand Teton and Yellowstone, Beartooth Highway to Montana, and return via I-90
assistant|route_option_utah_mighty_five: Suggested Option 2: Utah's Mighty Five — Moab, Arches, Canyonlands, Capitol Reef, Bryce Canyon, and Zion, returning via I-70
assistant|route_option_sierra_nevada: Suggested Option 3: California's Sierra Nevada — Yosemite, Sequoia, and Kings Canyon via I-80 to Sacramento (approx. 20 hours each way)
assistant|beartooth_highway_facts: The Beartooth Highway (US-212) is a 68-mile paved scenic road connecting Cooke City, Montana to Red Lodge, Montana through the Beartooth Mountains
assistant|beartooth_highway_conditions: The Beartooth Highway is generally in good condition from late May to early October, with speed limits of 45-65 mph and elevations over 10,000 feet
assistant|beartooth_highway_tips: Advised filling up on gas in Cooke City or Red Lodge since stations are limited, and checking the Montana DOT website for closures
assistant|colter_bay_campground: Colter Bay Campground is on the shores of Jackson Lake with 350 sites accommodating RVs/trailers up to 45 feet, flush toilets, showers, and potable water; reservations via recreation.gov
assistant|colter_bay_electric_sites: Colter Bay Campground has 100 sites with 30-amp electric hookups in the 'Electric Loop' section, for RVs/trailers up to 45 feet
assistant|colter_bay_reservation_window: Colter Bay Campground has a 6-month reservation window, so sites can be booked up to 6 months in advance via recreation.gov
assistant|colter_bay_water_dump: Colter Bay Campground has several potable water stations and a free dump station near the entrance for campers
assistant|jenny_lake_campground: Jenny Lake Campground near Moose has 49 sites for RVs/trailers up to 30 feet with flush toilets, showers, and potable water; reservations via recreation.gov
assistant|signal_mountain_campground: Signal Mountain Campground on Jackson Lake has 235 sites for RVs/trailers up to 30 feet with flush toilets, showers, and potable water; reservations via recreation.gov
assistant|granite_creek_campground: Granite Creek Campground in Bridger-Teton National Forest has 61 sites for RVs/trailers up to 40 feet with flush toilets, showers, and potable water
assistant|curtis_canyon_campground: Curtis Canyon Campground in Bridger-Teton National Forest has 12 sites for RVs/trailers up to 30 feet with vault toilets and potable water
assistant|jackson_hole_campground: Jackson Hole Campground at Fireside Resort in Wilson, Wyoming has 200 sites for all-size RVs/trailers with flush toilets, showers, pool, and Wi-Fi
assistant|virginian_lodge_rv_resort: Virginian Lodge RV Resort in Jackson, Wyoming has 230 sites for all-size RVs/trailers with flush toilets, showers, pool, hot tub, and Wi-Fi
assistant|camping_tips: Advised reserving campsites well in advance for peak season (June to August) and bringing bear spray in both parks
assistant|yellowstone_loop_details: Grand Teton offers scenic roads, hiking trails, and lakes; Yellowstone, America's first national park, is about 1 hour north with geysers, hot springs, wildlife, Old Faithful, and the Grand Prismatic Spring; the Beartooth Highway leg to Montana takes about 4 hours
assistant|beartooth_summer_weather: Summer weather on the Beartooth Highway is usually mild with average highs in the 60s-70s°F (15-21°C), though occasional thunderstorms can bring heavy rain and strong winds
assistant|beartooth_wildlife: The Beartooth Mountains are home to bears, elk, deer, and bighorn sheep; drivers should be extra cautious at dawn and dusk when animals are most active
assistant|beartooth_altitude: The Beartooth Highway reaches elevations over 10,000 feet (3,000 meters), which can cause altitude sickness; take regular breaks, stay hydrated, and watch for symptoms
assistant|park_summer_crowds: Summer is peak tourist season in Yellowstone and Grand Teton National Parks, so visitors should expect crowds and long lines at popular attractions
assistant|park_visitor_services: Both Yellowstone and Grand Teton offer free shuttle services, guided tours, and ranger programs that can enhance the experience and reduce congestion
assistant|colter_bay_facility_rules: Potable water is for refilling RV tanks only, not washing vehicles; the dump station is for RV waste only; campers should conserve water and follow grey/black water disposal guidelines
assistant|colter_bay_water_pressure: Water pressure at Colter Bay's potable water stations can be high, so campers should use a pressure regulator to avoid damaging their RV's plumbing
assistant|utah_mighty_five_details: Arches NP has over 2,000 natural arches; Canyonlands includes the Island in the Sky and The Needles districts; Bryce Canyon is known for unique hoodoos; drives between parks run 30 minutes to 2.5 hours
assistant|sierra_nevada_park_details: Yosemite features iconic landmarks like Half Dome and El Capitan; Sequoia NP has giant sequoia groves (about 4 hours from Yosemite); Kings Canyon has the deepest canyon in North America (about 1 hour further)
